locator.section: General Recommendations

definitions.text: Size is the average of the long- and short-axis diameters, measured on the same image (transverse, coronal or sagittal) showing the largest dimensions, rounded to the nearest millimetre. <6 mm means a rounded size of 5 mm or less.

locator.section: Risk Estimation and Risk Models

definitions.text: Low risk is an estimated cancer risk below 5% (younger age, less smoking, smaller size, regular margins, non-upper-lobe). High risk combines the ACCP intermediate (5–65%) and high (>65%) categories.

locator.section: Tobacco and Other Inhaled Carcinogens; Risk Estimation and Risk Models

definitions.text: High-risk factors include older age, heavy smoking (30 pack-years or more and quitting within the past 15 years, the NLST threshold), larger size, irregular or spiculated margins and upper lobe location.

locator.section: Nodule Size and Morphology

definitions.text: Subsolid nodules are ground-glass (no solid component) or part-solid. Components visible on mediastinal (soft-tissue) window settings are solid.

locator.section: Recommendation 2: multiple solid noncalcified nodules

definitions.text: With multiple nodules, the most suspicious (dominant) nodule guides management; it may not be the largest. The others are monitored on follow-up.

locator.section: Tobacco and Other Inhaled Carcinogens

definitions.text: Subsolid nodule recommendations do not depend on the customary risk categories.

locator.section: Table note; Introduction and Implications for Patient Care (p. 2)

pitfalls.text: Does not apply to lung cancer screening (use Lung-RADS), patients under 35, immunocompromised patients or patients with known primary cancer.

locator.section: General Recommendations

pitfalls.text: Volumetric thresholds (100 and 250 mm³) are given by the source but are not supported here yet; enter the average diameter.

locator.section: Figures 1 and 2

pitfalls.text: Applies to noncalcified nodules. Benign calcification patterns or fat (e.g. hamartoma, granuloma) need no CT follow-up.

locator.section: Perifissural Nodules

pitfalls.text: Perifissural or juxtapleural nodules with typical lymph node morphology need no follow-up, even above 6 mm; spiculation, fissure displacement or cancer history change this.

locator.section: Recommendation 4: solitary part-solid lung nodules

pitfalls.text: For part-solid nodules, the table size is the whole nodule; a solid component of 6 mm or more, or above 8 mm, changes management.

locator.section: Recommendation 2: multiple solid noncalcified nodules

pitfalls.text: The table has no row for a mix of solid and subsolid nodules; the source says the most suspicious nodule guides management.

locator.section: Incidentally Detected Lung Nodules on Incomplete Thoracic CT Scans

pitfalls.text: Nodules on partial chest CT (e.g. abdomen): <6 mm need no further imaging; 6–8 mm need complete chest CT at 3–12 months.

locator.section: General Recommendations

pitfalls.text: If the first scan used thick sections, a short-term thin-section follow-up may be needed before applying the table.

summary.text: Fleischner Society 2017 guidance for incidental pulmonary nodules on CT in adults aged 35 or over, revising the earlier Fleischner guidelines for solid and subsolid nodules.

locator.table: Fleischner Society 2017 Guidelines

summary.text: Management is set by nodule type (solid, ground-glass, part-solid), single or multiple, size, and for solid nodules the patient's clinical risk.

locator.section: Advances in Knowledge

summary.text: The threshold for routine follow-up of solid nodules is 6 mm; subsolid nodules are followed longer, up to 5 years.
Ranges of follow-up intervals are deliberate, leaving room for radiologist, clinician and patient preference.
